description: Spindle log retention policy. See docs/observability/log-retention.md for the rationale behind each threshold. Patterns are relative to the repo root (or --root). Age is measured from file mtime; '*.gz' files are only eligible for deletion, never re-compressed.

rules.name: secret-access-audit
rules.description: Secret access audit JSONL (.spindle/secret-access-audit.jsonl*). Contract requires >= 90 days of local history to cover the longest secret rotation max-age (Resend 180d provider overlap is covered by the shipped copy; local floor is the 90d EDGE_HMAC/B2/LLM/Postgres/Worker rotations). Compress after 30d, delete local copies after 365d once shipped to the central store per docs/security/secret-access-audit.md.

rules.name: app-json-logs
rules.description: Application pino JSON logs spilled to disk (logs/app/, logs/app.log*) and the ship.mjs file sink (logs/ship.jsonl* plus rotated .N files, or a logs/ship/ dir if --out points there). Primary store is Loki with 14d hot retention (docs/observability/log-aggregation.md); local spools are a buffer, so 30d is ample for gap recovery. Compress after 7d.

rules.name: access-logs
rules.description: nginx/edge-style access logs written to logs/nginx/ on the host (not the Cloudflare Tunnel — edge logs live in Cloudflare). 90d covers the 28d SLO windows in docs/slo/service-level-objectives.md plus investigation margin; keepNewest protects the active file from age-based deletion.

rules.name: deploy-logs
rules.description: Deploy/rollback operator logs (logs/deploy/). Deploy history of record lives in GitHub Actions artifacts and scripts/deploy/rollback.mjs release records; local copies are debugging aids. 90d matches the quarterly DR drill cadence in docs/resilience/disaster-recovery.md.

rules.name: misc-logs
rules.description: Catch-all for other host-side *.log/*.jsonl under logs/ not claimed above (e.g. /var/log/spindle-backup.log copied into logs/). Conservative 90d.

rules.name: backup-artifacts
rules.description: pg_dump artifacts in backups/ (spindle-*). Count-based retention (keep newest 14, or BACKUP_RETENTION_COUNT) is owned by scripts/db/backup/backup.ts — this rule is only a 400d age safety net so a forgotten cron cannot accumulate dumps forever. keepNewest mirrors the default count retention as a second guard.
